finalJustifications: Because the DLQ in SQS holds the failed events in a durable way to reprocess later — and Archive+Replay sends whole batches back when the bank returns.
Because the DLQ of the EventBridge monitors the health check of the external database and redelivers the events as soon as it responds.
Because the Archive freezes the Lambda at the point of failure and Replay resumes execution exactly of the call that was interrupted.
Because the line SQS assumes the role of the bank during the inavailability, responding to queries with the data stored in it.

optionReasons.saa-med-249:option:1: It is the closest because this parameter exists and in fact limits the parallelism of that integration — but controls only the POLLING of the row: the function remains free to scale from other sources, and the scenario asks to limit the processing rate of the function itself; the classic and comprehensive brake is the Reserved Competition.

finalJustifications: Because Reserved Competition puts a ceiling on parallel performance of the function: with all the instances occupied, the SQS wait — the flow is limited and the waterfall stops.
Because Reserved Competition reserves exclusive instances for the queue, processing accumulated messages in order of arrival.
Because Reserved Competition returns messages above the limit with a new exponential delay calculated by Lambda.
Because Reserved Competition pauses the Event Source Mapping when the downstream saturates, resuming the polling in her recovery.

(Exclude invalid specific VERSSION would work — not what the option describes.) The supported stream is copy the previous version back..
optionReasons.saa-med-251:option:2: Replication is for those who set it up ANTES — and also replicates the overwritten; it is not local version recovery mechanism.
optionReasons.saa-med-251:option:3: There is no lifecycle guarantee for Glacier on the stage — and the version already saves the previous version in the pocket itself.

finalJustifications: Because with versioning the previous version follows in the bucket: just locate it (ListObjectVersions) and copy it back as current version.
Because ListObjectVersions includes a rollback command that promotes the chosen version without creating a new copy in the pocket.
Because CopyObject with VersionId mixes the two versions, recovering the valid blocks from the overwritten file by the script.
Because the console of S3 keeps a trash can 30 days per versioned bucket, and the restoration is made directly from there.

optionReasons.saa-med-254:option:0: Batch size maximum is 10.000 only with batching window and does not eliminate throttling — and a giant batch that fails reprocesses everything again.
optionReasons.saa-med-254:option:1: It's the closest because long polling is real good practice and reduces empty chicks — but efficiency of POLL does not prevent EXPIRY: with the competition blown, messages continue to age until retention wins; what avoids loss is to retain for longer (14 days) + DLQ.
optionReasons.saa-med-254:option:2: FIFO does not eliminate throttling — still reduces throughput; and duplicates are not the cause of the limit of competition.

finalJustifications: Because the retention of even 14 days gives time for messages to wait for competition to free, and the DLQ captures those that fail repeatedly — nothing expires lost.
Because the major retention activates the priority queue of the SQS, processed before new messages at each traffic peak.
Because the DLQ absorbs the excess of throttling and forwards it to Lambda in reduced rate, within the limit of competition.
Because the retention of 14 days freezes the visibility timeout of pending payments, preventing any new expiration.

finalJustifications: Because the roof of 29s is hard limit of API Gateway: Long operations saw asynchronous — 202 Accepted immediately, processing in background and polling/WebSocket.
Because the limit of 29s is elevated by Service Quotas, and the asynchronous pattern is only necessary above the 120 approved seconds.
Because 202 Accepted instructed or API Gateway keeping the connection open beyond the 29s up to Lambda complete all work.
Because the asynchronous pattern transfers the timeout to the client, who sets the maximum deadline by the header of the request sent.

optionReasons.saa-med-259:option:2: One Zone-IA reduces durability (one AZ) and also collects retrieval — backups of reprocessed analytics do not fit.

finalJustifications: Because Intelligent-Tiering moves each object between third parties by real use — without manual rule, without retriival rate — the exact unpredictable standard fit.
Because the Intelligent-Tiering predicts with ML which objects will be re-accessed and promotes them to the warm ter before the demand arrives.
Because Intelligent-Tiering charges average single rate per GB, always lower than any fixed storage class.
Because the Intelligent-Tiering replicates the cold objects to the Glacier keeping a hot copy, and the reading never pays waits.

finalJustifications: Because Parquet/ORC read only the columns used (column pruning) and the partitions by date limit the scan to the filtered days — the double that drops GB scanned and cost.
Because the Parquet indexes the logs in a catalog of Athena, which responds to direct index queries without touching the index files S3.
Because partitioning distributes the wants among more us of Athena, and extra parallelism reduces time without changing the cost.
Because the column format caches the results per column in Athena, and the following will pay only the new columns.
